result:
Round 322 is stopped and needs a B ruling. A test outside my grant blocks it, and fixing that test in place would mean inverting an assertion. Nothing in `store/` changed after I hit the stop, and the tree is consistent.

**The blocker.** `render-budget.test.tsx` is one of the 81 files that had to pass with no edit. At l.616–620 it uses `selectClip` as its positive control: it asserts that a selection change gives a new context value and re-renders all five consumers. PERF-8b removes exactly that link, so the test fails at l.617. The §2.4 exception covers only reading selection fields, so it doesn't apply here. B's precheck couldn't catch this: on the type-only sketch all 81 files crashed before reaching that line.

**Proposed ruling (a).** Grant that one test, switch the positive control to `setStatus(...)`, and add a negative check: `selectClip` leaves the value unchanged and Ruler and Library at 0 renders. No assertion is removed; the file gains 3 `expect(`. I ran this edit on a scratch copy of my tree outside `store/` and the file passed 8/8. The exact edit is quoted in the report, because the scratch folder won't survive the job.

**What's already in the tree (all within the granted files):**
- The new `selection-store.ts`: one store per provider, and same ids in a different order still count as a change.
- The context no longer holds the selection: it is gone from the value, its deps, `latestRef` and `useState`, and the 14 handler reads use `getSelectedClipIds()`.
- Transport reads one "a clip is selected" flag. Each lane re-renders only when its own clips' selection changes.
- `StudioWorkspace` no longer subscribes to the selection. Four small subscriber components inside it now handle what reads it: the "n clips selected" count, the selected-clip line, the group header and the detail panel.
- The 29 test files: only the way they read the selection changed.

**Checks I actually ran:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Claims before editing | Identical to HEAD |
| Claims now | K3, K4, K5, K10, K11 at 0; K12 at 1; protected files 11/11 OK |
| `npm run typecheck` | rc 0 |
| `npm run lint` | rc 0; the 205 warnings are repo-wide, none in my files |
| `expect(` count, 29 files | Unchanged at 4,021 |
| Covering tests (111 files) | 110 passed, 1 failed (the blocker); 1704/1705 tests |
| Click probe, same-lane select (dev server) | Provider doesn't render, none of the 10 names, 23 components (HEAD 105) |
| Click probe, re-click | 0 components, but still 1 empty commit; HEAD makes that empty commit too |
| Add-video probe (S2) | 0 commits showing the old selection after the range cleared (HEAD 2) |

C's SELECT-NAMES row asks for 0 commits on a re-click, which can't pass while that empty commit exists on HEAD too. In the report I propose rewording it to "0 components rendered, at most 1 commit".

**Not done yet, until the ruling:** the SS1–SS7 test file, the four mutants, the harness rows (K19 is still 0), docs 168/230/231, the perf run and the code-reviewer. I held the review back because the change set isn't final. I also didn't run `perf/lib/report.test.ts`. No acceptance rows are claimed beyond those run above.

**Architecture note for B:** the four subscriber components add about 190 lines to `StudioWorkspace.tsx`. Later they could move next to the components they wrap, which are outside this round's grants.

C has nothing to verify this round. Everything is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-322.md`, with logs and probe output in `a-round-322/`.
